title: Slice-aware fractional rollout policy and automatic rollback heuristics
creator: Liam Chen
description: Introduce a slice-aware fractional exposure policy and an associated set of automatic rollback heuristics. The goal is to allow canary/A-B/shadow experiments to define targeted slices (region, customer_tier, device_family, traffic_source) with independent traffic fractions and safety limits. The engine should enforce per-slice and global guardrails, compute step schedules (time or successful-sample driven), blend shadow probes without affecting live traffic, and trigger deterministic rollbacks when quality or infrastructure SLOs regress beyond configured thresholds.
acceptance_criteria: Policy DSL supports declaration of arbitrary slices with selectors (e.g., country, plan, user_cohort) and assigns independent fraction schedules.
Runtime enforces per-slice guardrails (error_rate, latency_p95, model_quality_score) and prevents step progression when violated.
Automatic rollback triggers based on configurable heuristics (absolute thresholds, relative delta vs baseline, sustained degradation window).
Shadow probe mode sends mirrored requests at configured fraction and labels observability without impacting production quotas or billing.
End-to-end integration tests validate a canary scenario with three slices (US, EU, APAC) and confirm safe rollback on simulated regressions.
Performance overhead of policy enforcement on request path < 3% median latency increase in benchmark harness.
implementation_notes: Add policy compiler that converts DSL into per-node runtime checks and a lightweight token-bucket for fractional sampling.
Reuse existing routing layer hooks to apply slice selectors before kernel scheduling to avoid extra hop.
Implement guardrail evaluator as streaming rule engine that consumes model telemetry and infra SLO metrics.
Expose a /v1/policy/evaluate endpoint for Console and test harness to query current step and blocked reason.
Prefer eventual consistency for non-critical metrics, but ensure immediate enforcement for rollback triggers.
Provide a canary-simulator tool to run deterministic experiments in CI using synthetic telemetry bursts.
config_example:
# Example policy (YAML-like)
policy_name: slice_fractional_exposure_v1
description: Fractional rollout with per-slice guardrails and automatic rollback heuristics
slices:
  - name: us_web_users
    selector: country=US && device=web
    schedule:
      - step: 0
        fraction: 0.01
        duration_minutes: 60
      - step: 1
        fraction: 0.05
        duration_minutes: 120
      - step: 2
        fraction: 0.25
        duration_minutes: 360
    guardrails:
      latency_p95_ms: 750
      error_rate_pct: 0.7
      quality_score_delta: -0.02
  - name: eu_mobile_premium
    selector: region=EU && plan=premium && device=mobile
    schedule:
      - step: 0
        fraction: 0.005
        duration_minutes: 120
      - step: 1
        fraction: 0.02
        duration_minutes: 240
    guardrails:
      latency_p95_ms: 850
      error_rate_pct: 1.0
      quality_score_delta: -0.01
global_guardrails:
  max_global_fraction: 0.3
  global_latency_p95_ms: 900
  sustained_window_minutes: 30
rollback_heuristics:
  - name: absolute_error_threshold
    metric: error_rate_pct
    threshold: 2.0
    sustained_minutes: 5
  - name: relative_quality_drop
    metric: quality_score_delta
    compare_to: baseline_revision
    relative_threshold: -0.03
    sustained_minutes: 15
shadow_probe:
  enabled: true
  fraction: 0.02
  isolation: true  # mirrored responses ignored for billing and production counters
progression_policy:
  mode: time_based # or success_sample_based
  min_successful_samples: 1000
  step_backoff_on_failure_minutes: 30
telemetry_checks: Per-slice metrics: request_count, error_rate_pct, latency_p50/95/99, model_quality_score (from eval hooks)
Baseline comparison: compare canary slice metrics to pinned baseline model revision for percent delta calculations.
Infra SLOs: GPU_util_pct, queue_length, request_processing_errors must be observed and mapped to rollback triggers.
Shadow probe hygiene: ensure mirrored requests have no side effects and are tagged for cost-exemption.
testing_plan: Unit tests for policy compiler and guardrail evaluator with synthetic metric streams.
Integration test using canary-simulator where we inject a quality regression and assert rollback occurs within config window.
Staging A/B run with one model variant receiving slice traffic; measure overhead and telemetry fidelity.
Chaos test: simulate overloaded GPU nodes and assert policy does not progress and appropriately throttles rollout.
E2E runbook validation: verify Console shows blocked reason and allows manual override with audit trail.
risks: Incorrect slice selectors could lead to unintended traffic shifts — need thorough selector validation and dry-run mode.
Telemetry delays can cause premature rollbacks or delayed detection — add configurable grace windows and smoothing.
Overly-complex DSL may be hard for PMs to author; provide opinionated templates and Console UX for common patterns.
Performance impact of per-request checks if implemented synchronously — benchmark and use fast-path caching for stable state.
